title: The ring a guide draws matches the shape it is drawn round
goal: When a tutorial puts a highlight ring on a control, the ring should take the shape of that control. Today it is always a rounded rectangle with the same corner radius, so on the pill shaped floating tool bar the corners do not line up with the thing they are ringing.
notes:
Evidence: queue/audits/2026-09-12-tutorials-01-tool-bar.png shows the ring round the tool bar with a 10pt corner radius against the bar own pill. Ran Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/tutorial-tour-walk.json and read the first capture.

The radius is hard coded at the one call site: TutorialController.placeCue passes TutorialCueView(cornerRadius: 10). The anchor itself is the only thing that knows its shape, so the shape probably has to travel with the anchor: either a corner radius on TutorialAnchor, or a small shape enum set where the anchor is hung. See docs/design/tutorials.md.
acceptance: The ring round the floating tool bar is a pill, matching the bar
The ring round a round tool button is round
The ring round a panel section keeps the squarer corner it has now
A walk captures each of the three and the audit shows them side by side

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock's .wt-cue is one fixed rounded box, and building it literally is exactly what the complaint is about, so the mock is wrong here and the app follows the control instead. Rejected two shortcuts. (1) Measuring the control's corner at draw time: nothing on screen will tell you what radius a SwiftUI view was drawn with, so it would have been a guess dressed up as a measurement. (2) A shape passed in at each .tutorialAnchor(...) call site: 23 call sites, every one a chance to hang the wrong shape, and a step written for an anchor would have no way to know what it will get. The shape belongs to the anchor, which is the one value both ends already share.

Shipped: TutorialCueShape in PhotonzCore (.pill or .rounded(radius), plus outset(by:) which keeps the ring concentric with the control instead of letting its corner tighten as it goes out), read off the anchor name by TutorialAnchor.cueShape so an anchor off disk rings the same as one the app just built. TutorialCueView now takes the shape and draws Capsule() or RoundedRectangle; TutorialController.placeCue re-applies it every placement through a new cueHost, which the old code could not do because it built the ring's view once and never touched it again.

Verification: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so every walk reports locked and exits 3 and nothing could be photographed. Acceptance 4 (a walk capturing the three side by side) is therefore NOT met by a walk; a sweep has been requested and will run the tutorial walks once the screen is unlocked. Instead the shipping TutorialCueView source was compiled into a standalone ImageRenderer harness and drawn round stand-ins of the three controls: queue/audits/2026-09-16-tutorial-ring-shapes.png shows a pill on the bar, a circle on the tool button, and the same 10pt corner on the panel section. That is the real drawing code, not a mock of it, but the surroundings are stand-ins. Harness was throwaway (/tmp/cue-render: main.swift plus the view's source appended, linked against .build PhotonzCore objects) and is not checked in.

left rough: the toolBar anchor sits on the container holding BOTH the tools capsule and the tool settings capsules beside it, so one pill rings the pair across the gap between them. Closer than the old box but not exact; did not earn its own task (nobody is stopped by it and the audit's rough list carries it for the user to react to).
